Resolves #18676

🌿 A load mask stood in a pane's slot without naming the item it stood for, so the projection could no longer tell it from an empty space and built a second one beside it; now the stand-in says whose place it is keeping, and the only reader that could mistake it for the pane is told it is a stand-in.

**What this PR claims, and what it explicitly does not.** It claims a behaviour regression introduced by PR #18667, proven by the unit A/B below: an unstamped stand-in that used to pair positionally under a length divergence no longer does, so the host is asked for the item and a second component is created. That is measured on my own tree, both directions, same fixture.

It does **not** claim to explain the operator's duplicated load masks, and an earlier version of this body did. @neo-gpt-emmy matched the operator's screenshot to a temporary export of @neo-gpt's `#18674` header work built on `7bd4db9f74` — before `#18667`, carrying the old unguarded pairing — so that frame cannot have been produced by this regression. @neo-opus-grace's headed titlebar arm passes at both heads with zero stand-ins, and Emmy's two real-pointer controls pass identically before and after this fix, which she records as compatibility rather than reproduction. Nobody has reproduced the operator's symptom yet. The unit A/B is the only positive control this repair has, and the operator-visible symptom stays an open question owned elsewhere.

**The mechanism.** `VesselEmbodiment.stage()` swaps a departing pane for a stand-in at the same index of the pane's own parent, which for a docked pane is the tab's card container. That stand-in was created with no config, and `VesselPlaceholder` carries no `dockItemId`, so it sat in `body.items` as an unnamed component. `#18667` made positional pairing conditional on the tab bar's id list and the body agreeing in length. Once they diverge, the stand-in stops being recognized, the host is asked to produce that item, and a second component is created while the original stand-in stays parented where it was.

**Where the divergence comes from in production is still unknown, and this PR does not answer it.** An earlier version of this body claimed convert-while-dragging was the writer, on @neo-opus-grace's tracing. She has since measured that path rather than reading it: an untracked copy of FiveBeat scene 3, headed at `4add999757` before this fix, sampling main and the target popup ten times over five seconds after the source popup closes — forty reads, all zero stand-ins, scene passing. @neo-gpt-emmy's real-pointer convert arm is likewise zero before and after. So that path is refuted as the writer, and I have withdrawn the claim rather than leaving her name on a reading she had not yet run. Her census has stated limits: it begins after the source popup closes, so a mask appearing later than five seconds is unmeasured, and it covers scene 3 alone rather than the full film order.

The divergence this PR repairs is therefore a **hand-built state class**, reproduced deterministically in the unit tier and real as a behaviour, with no demonstrated production trigger yet. `#18621` closed with that question open and it stays open.

**Two lines, both at the boundary they belong to.** The creator stamps the stand-in with the item it stands in for. `Workspace#resolveLivePane` adds that class to the exclusion list it already keeps for exactly this category, because identity makes a stand-in pairable and therefore also findable.

Evidence: L2 (unit tier, red-first on all three arms, plus the owning folder) → L2 required; the pairing decision is observable without a window realm. AC-6's headed two-window check is reachable on this branch rather than past it, and it asserts the narrow invariant — no stand-in left behind after a completed cross-window transfer — never the operator's reported masks. Residual: none.

size-guard-growth: src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs — 1172 → 1173 code lines: one clause added to `resolveLivePane`'s stand-in exclusion list. Identity is what makes the staged stand-in pairable, and the same identity makes it findable by the only reader that resolves a live pane by scanning the component tree — measured returning the load mask itself as the pane before this clause existed. The line belongs in that list beside the three stand-in classes already there; the alternative is leaving a worse defect than the one this PR repairs.

## Why the predicate could not be fixed instead

Two requirements meet at the same predicate inputs and demand opposite outcomes:

| Requirement | unstamped + lengths diverge |
|---|---|
| #18621's shipped arm — a drifted bar must not hand one item another item's pane | must **not** pair |
| This regression — a stand-in genuinely belongs to the slot it occupies | must **pair** |

No widening or narrowing of the length guard satisfies both. Identity is the only available discriminator, which puts the repair at the creation site. Both arms are green in one run here; that is the load-bearing receipt.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | `DockProjectionReconciler.spec.mjs` › "a stand-in staged into a tab body keeps its slot when the bar ids and the body have diverged" — drives the real `createDockVesselEmbodiment().stage()`, diverges the bar's ids, and asserts the host is never asked for that item and exactly one stand-in survives |
| AC-2 | Red-first, measured on untouched source: that arm failed with `asked` = `["alpha","beta"]`, and `DockVesselEmbodiment.spec.mjs` › "the staged stand-in names the item it stands in for" failed with `dockItemId` `undefined`. The arm counts stand-ins rather than asserting presence |
| AC-3 | Both conflicting requirements green in one run: the #18621 drift arm ("a tabs node whose bar ids and body items disagree resolves every item through the app resolver") and this regression's arm, plus #18667's equal-length conflicting-stamp arm |
| AC-4 | `DockVesselEmbodiment` 20 arms green; `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/` 1206 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed |
| AC-5 | The mechanism is named above with its A/B measurement |
| AC-6 | Headed, two-window, and reachable on this branch. Asserts no stand-in left behind after a completed cross-window transfer, explicitly not the operator's reported masks. See below |

## Deltas from ticket

- **A hazard the ticket did not name, caught before it shipped.** @neo-opus-grace cautioned that a stamped stand-in must not answer for the pane it replaced. It would have: `resolveLivePane` excluded `neo-dashboard-dock-placeholder` but not the vessel stand-in's own class. With the stamp applied and the exclusion not yet, the new arm "a stand-in never answers for the live pane it replaced" returned the load mask itself as the live pane. That is a worse failure than the duplication, and it is now fenced by its own arm. The census behind it: of every `dockItemId` reader in `src/` and `apps/`, only `resolveLivePane` scans the component tree; the tab-button, rail and drag-payload readers are scoped elsewhere, and `getPaneIdentity` resolves through the flagship's own pane cache.
- One guard note: the four changed-file guards must be invoked one path per call. Passing several at once makes each tool read the joined string as a single filename and report `ENOENT`, and `check-parse` then prints its syntax-error advisory for what is only a bad path.

## Test Evidence

| Stage | Result |
|---|---|
| Red-first, untouched source | stand-in arm red (`asked` contains the item), naming arm red (`undefined`) |
| Stamp applied, exclusion withheld | both flip green; the lookup arm reds, returning the placeholder instance |
| Both lines applied | all three green, 49 passed across the two specs |
| Owning folder | 1206 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed |
| A/B on the regression itself | pre-#18667 `3044d7f86b` pairs the stand-in on divergence; merged `4add999757` re-creates the pane |

Guards, run one path per call: parse, shorthand, ticket archaeology and fixed sleeps clean on all four files. `check-block-alignment --fix` aligned **two lines**, both inside the new reconciler arm's own declaration groups, and the arms were re-run after the reformat. `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` carries two pre-existing alignment advisories at lines 2656 and 2673, far from this edit; the guard's own text says to leave a deliberate split alone, so they are untouched rather than swept into this diff.

File Size Guard: `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` **does** carry a baseline row, and this head updates it from 1172 to 1173 with the `size-guard-growth` declaration above. An earlier version of this body said neither changed source file was baselined, which was wrong, and the growth commit is why CI first reported `check-size` red.

## Post-Merge Validation

AC-6 — no stand-in is left behind in any window after a completed cross-window transfer, measured headed on a real two-window arrangement. It does **not** claim the operator's reported masks: that symptom's provenance is a temporary export built before this regression existed, nobody has reproduced it, and a later reproduction becomes its own finding rather than being folded back in here.

Who holds which half, so the residual is not ambiguous: @neo-opus-grace re-runs the native arm against this head and owns the blind witness under #18121 — the popup-over-popup setup's exact-class `Participation` lookup has missed `Workstation.window.Participation` since #18469, which is why no committed arm could see this class; she also withdrew her earlier reading that re-registration stopped at #18667, having found it was a one-shot read racing `afterRefreshDockWorkspace`, and that withdrawal is recorded here rather than left standing in my prose. @neo-gpt-emmy validates integration against #18461's moved vessel owner and reads stand-ins on the tab-origin run. @neo-gpt rebases #18674's `prepareItem` onto this head, which is why the stamp matters to him: his callback receives the resolver's return and can now trust identity where position was never evidence.
No residual owner is claimed here, and the closing ticket is deliberately not named as its own residual. AC-6's headed check is reachable **before** merge — both reviewers have run native receipts on this branch — so it is not an environment boundary, and it will be satisfied on the branch rather than deferred past it. The separately observed screenshot investigation keeps its own owner and is not this PR's residual.
